title: A tenth
hookLine: the tradition of giving a tenth of income
tomorrow: Noa has her tenth. a check, or something better?

cards: A first paycheck has a weight to it, even as a number on a screen. It's yours; you earned every hour. So why would anyone hand back a tenth?

Go back to Jacob, running from his brother, asleep on the ground with a stone under his head. He dreams of a ladder with angels going up and down, and wakes up shaken. He owns nothing but what he's carrying.
Then he makes a promise about money he doesn't have yet. In the JPS 1917 translation: "of all that Thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto Thee."

teach.h: ALL THAT THOU SHALT GIVE ME.
teach.b: Listen for the word give, twice. Jacob calls everything he'll ever earn something given, and the tenth is his way of saying so out loud.

teach.h: HARVESTS FOR THE STRANGER AND THE WIDOW.
teach.b: In the Torah, tithes were harvests: grain, wine and oil set apart, and in the third year a tithe left in town for the Levite, the stranger, the orphan and the widow, so they could eat and be satisfied.
Later teachers carried the tenth over to money. It's called ma'aser kesafim, a tenth of money, and teachers differ on whether it's a law or a strong custom.

teach.h: A FIFTH, A TENTH, A STINGY EYE.
teach.b: The Shulchan Aruch, a code of Jewish law, lays out a scale: up to a fifth is the finest way to give, a tenth is the middle way, and less than that is a stingy eye. Here's what a tenth can do that a good mood can't.
It's a number, so it doesn't wait until you feel generous. It shrinks when you earn little and grows when you earn more.
And it comes off the top, before the money is spent, so what you give isn't leftovers.
Something to tell a friend tonight: Jacob made this promise before he had a single thing to tithe.

how: Many observant Jews set aside ma'aser, a tenth of their income, for tzedakah; some keep a separate account or jar for it and decide during the year where it goes.

o: a tenth set apart from what you earn, given first
the tenth day of a month, kept as a fast
a yearly fee paid to keep a synagogue seat

p: the tenth of all that is given
the finest way, says the Shulchan Aruch

s: Jacob promised a tenth once he had grown rich
he vowed it on the run, with nothing, about what he would be given later.
ma'aser is a membership fee paid to a synagogue
it's a tenth given to tzedakah: the poor and good causes.
the Shulchan Aruch calls up to a fifth the finest way to give
a tenth is the middle way; less is a stingy eye.

games.q: your sister earns a little from babysitting and says she'll start giving a tenth once it's real money. what does the tenth itself answer?
o: a tenth scales: small when you earn little, bigger when you earn more.
she's right: the tithe only starts above a certain income.
she should give all of it until she can afford a proper tenth.
games.why: a tenth is a share, not an amount, so it fits any paycheck. Jacob vowed it before he had anything at all.

practice: Set out ten small things in a row: coins, beans, paper clips. Touch each one as you count it, and feel how alike they are.
Then slide one a little apart from the others, and rest your eyes on the nine still in front of you, and the one that already belongs to someone else.

wordCard.voice: Ma'aser: a tenth, set apart first. In the Torah, a tenth of the harvest; later, a tenth of money, given to tzedakah.

orig.note: Hebrew: a tenth; the tithe set apart from a harvest, and later from income.

carryVoice: For your pocket: give a tenth, off the top, the way Jacob promised with empty hands. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: of all that Thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto Thee

sources.ref: Genesis 28:10–22 (Jacob's flight, the stone, the dream of the ladder, the vow)
Deuteronomy 14:22–29 (the yearly tithe; the third-year tithe for the Levite, stranger, fatherless and widow)
Shulchan Aruch, Yoreh De'ah 249:1 (up to a fifth is the choicest way, a tenth the middle, less a stingy eye)
